title: QuickOps: ephemeral adminlets with provenance-tracing and staged approvals
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight ephemeral adminlet runner that lets on-call engineers execute small, parametrized maintenance actions as versioned tasks with end-to-end provenance, an approval staging flow, and a mandatory dry-run mode. Goal: reduce time-to-remediate frequent low-risk incidents while preserving auditability and safety.
background: On-call frequently runs repeated small fixes (rotate keys, clear cache shards, requeue jobs, or restart ephemeral workers). Current runbooks are prose-heavy and manual; copy-paste shell commands increase blast radius and make post-incident review difficult. Existing runbook-as-task efforts focus on large playbooks; there is a gap for tiny, high-frequency ops actions that must remain safe and traceable.
technical_design: Core components: (1) ephemeral adminlet registry: a typed manifest (YAML) for tiny actions with inputs, preconditions, and rollback hints; (2) runner service: executes adminlets inside a sandboxed helper pod with scoped credentials fetched from the RBAC service and KMS-wrapped secrets; (3) provenance tracer: immutable record capturing input values, template version, checksums, execution plan, stdout/stderr, and exit codes, stored in the audit store; (4) staged approvals: policy layer that enforces dry-run and auto-approve thresholds (e.g., no external-network mutations auto-approved) and allows on-call lead sign-off for elevated actions; (5) telemetry hooks export metrics: run_count, median_latency, failure_rate, and cost_estimate via existing admin-telemetry pipeline. The runner reuses our existing step-execution primitives (ENG-314271) but restricts surface area and enforces idempotency checks before execution. Rolling code path uses feature-flag gated canary execution and records a provenance snapshot to the admin-logs S3 bucket.
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal alpha (team-only) deploy to staging with follow mode (dry-run always enabled). Phase B: limited on-call beta with policy set to require a single approver for non-idempotent adminlets. Phase C: open to all on-call, with metrics dashboards and automated pruning of adminlets older than 90 days. Each phase will last at least 2 weeks and must meet acceptance criteria before advancing. Feature flag: ff/quickops/ephemeral-runner.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest validation and input sanitizers. Integration tests spin up sandboxed runner pods in CI using test harness with fake KMS and RBAC. End-to-end smoke tests run against a dedicated staging cluster; two curated runbooks will be executed in dry-run and live-run modes. Canary will run 5% of dev traffic for 3 days and collect success/failure logs. Incident simulation: use ops-playback tool to replay common on-call scenarios and verify provenance capture and rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adminlet manifest schema v1 validated by CI and documented.
- Dry-run produces deterministic execution plan without mutating targets.
- Provenance records created for every execution and queryable from admin-console (search by request id).
- RBAC policies enforced: non-approved users cannot execute adminlets that mutate prod state.
- Failure rate for included canary adminlets < 2% over 72h.
- Playbook examples migrated: at least 3 frequent fixes converted and approved by SRE.
notes: Trade-offs considered: embedded scripting languages (Lua) were rejected due to sandboxing complexity; instead we prefer small compiled helpers and a thin YAML manifest to reduce TCB. We debated allowing arbitrary templates vs typed args; typed args chosen to enable static validation and better telemetry. Long-run: consider uploading verified binary artifacts for cryptographic provenance.
